macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stock futures rise ahead of bank earnings and inflation data
items.summary: U.S. stock futures climbed Monday, with S&P 500 futures up 0.33%, Nasdaq 100 futures up 0.45% and Dow futures up 0.35%. Investors are focused on major bank earnings and this week’s inflation and retail-sales reports.[5]

items.title: Wall Street’s rally faces tests from CPI and bank results
items.summary: Investors are awaiting September CPI data, due Wednesday, and quarterly results from major banks including JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Wells Fargo. Economists expect headline inflation of roughly 3.6%–3.7% year over year and core inflation of 2.5%.[1][2]

items.title: Fed rate-hike expectations remain subdued before October meeting
items.summary: Markets are pricing only a 19% probability of a Federal Reserve rate increase at the October 27–28 meeting, while investors monitor CPI, producer prices and retail sales for signals about the interest-rate path.[8]

items.title: Major U.S. indexes posted gains last week
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 1.2%, the Dow gained 0.9% and the Nasdaq advanced 0.6% last week, while the Russell 2000 fell 0.9%. The S&P 500 had recently reached a record closing high as investors anticipated strong AI-related earnings.[10]

items.title: Oil volatility and geopolitical developments remain market risks
items.summary: Oil prices fluctuated around elevated levels as investors assessed geopolitical developments and a reported U.S.-Russia diesel-supply arrangement. Higher energy prices could add to headline inflation and keep pressure on bond yields and equity valuations.[8]

items.title: Bank earnings launch the third-quarter reporting season
items.summary: JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Wells Fargo are scheduled to report Tuesday, followed by Bank of America and Morgan Stanley Wednesday. ASML and TSMC are also scheduled to provide important semiconductor-sector updates later in the week.[2]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Ripple patches critical XRP Ledger bug
items.summary: Ripple said a critical software flaw that could have threatened XRP’s fixed supply was addressed before exploitation.

items.title: Bitcoin rises above $84,000
items.summary: Bitcoin traded above $84,000, up approximately 1.17% over 24 hours. The broader market remained mixed, with notable gains in several altcoins.

items.title: Starknet token surges on quantum-resistant blockchain plan
items.summary: Starknet’s STRK token reportedly jumped more than 44% after the network outlined a potential transition toward a quantum-resistant Layer 1 architecture.

items.title: Celestia rises after throughput and mainnet developments
items.summary: Celestia’s TIA token gained nearly 20% following reported progress on Celestia Fibre throughput and the launch of its Sustainable Blob feature.

items.title: CFTC chair proposes federal registration for some crypto exchanges
items.summary: CFTC Chairman Michael Selig proposed federal registration for certain cryptocurrency exchanges, including stronger market oversight and segregated customer funds.

items.title: Argentina pauses crypto integration with banks and payments
items.summary: Argentina’s central bank said it does not plan to integrate cryptocurrencies or digital assets into banking and payment channels during the next two years; existing restrictions remain in force.

items.title: Russia imposes stricter electricity terms on crypto miners
items.summary: Russia’s Energy Ministry said crypto miners seeking grid access must use a lower-priority reliability category, allowing authorities to disconnect them during power shortages.

items.title: Ethereum Foundation transfers 4,393 ETH to Kraken
items.summary: The Ethereum Foundation reportedly moved 4,393 ETH to Kraken, prompting market speculation about the potential implications for selling pressure.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: GTA 6 leaker links alleged full-game release to cryptocurrency target
items.summary: An anonymous GTA 6 leaker reportedly said a full development build would be released if a connected Solana token reached a $30 million market value. Rockstar continues to list Grand Theft Auto VI for November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.[1]

items.title: Ace Combat 8 surpasses one million sales
items.summary: Ace Combat 8: Skies Unknown reportedly passed one million copies sold within a week, making it the fastest-selling entry in the series, according to GameMAG.[2]

items.title: Forza Horizon 6 confirmed for PlayStation 5
items.summary: Microsoft and Playground Games announced that Forza Horizon 6 will launch on PlayStation 5 on January 26, 2027, alongside its first expansion and a free update.[2][5]

items.title: Rainbow Six Mobile support to end in January 2027
items.summary: Ubisoft and Vantage Studios announced that support for the free-to-play Rainbow Six Mobile will be discontinued, with servers scheduled to close on January 15, 2027.[2]

items.title: AION 2 exceeds 400,000 peak concurrent players
items.summary: NCSoft said AION 2 surpassed 400,000 peak concurrent players after its global launch on October 5; SteamDB recorded nearly 398,000 concurrent Steam players.[5]

items.title: 2026 League of Legends World Championship schedule announced
items.summary: The 2026 League of Legends World Championship will begin October 16 in Los Angeles and conclude with the November 15 final in New York, featuring 19 teams from six regions.[5]

items.title: Deadlock reaches new concurrent-player record
items.summary: Valve’s in-development multiplayer game Deadlock reportedly exceeded 260,000 peak concurrent players on Steam on October 9.[5]

items.title: 2026 Golden Joystick Awards shortlist revealed
items.summary: The shortlist for the publicly voted categories at the 44th annual Golden Joystick Awards has been announced, with voting now open.[7]

items.title: South Korean game-industry outlook turns negative
items.summary: South Korea’s game-industry business sentiment outlook for the fourth quarter fell to 99.2 from 100.0, as strong performance by major companies contrasted with continuing weakness among smaller and midsize studios.[9]
